references.text: Moses carries out the Lord's command to consecrate the people, and they wash their clothes, as a direct fulfillment of this verse.
God's call to holiness for His people: 'You shall be holy, for I am holy' - the theological basis for sanctification in Exodus 19:10.
Washing of clothes as part of the cleansing ritual, the same practice commanded in Exodus 19:10.
Joshua commands the people to consecrate themselves before the Lord's miraculous deeds, a similar preparation as at Sinai.
Command to consecrate the people before an important event with the Lord, the same pattern as in Exodus 19:10.
Samuel consecrated Jesse and his sons, the same sanctification practice that Moses carried out with the people.
Encouragement to approach God with a pure heart and body washed with clean water, a New Testament parallel to physical and spiritual cleansing.
Those who have washed their robes and made them white, an eschatological fulfillment of the cleansing motif from Sinai.
Blessed are those who wash their robes to gain the right to the tree of life, an end-time perspective on sanctification and cleansing.
Describes the direct fulfillment of the command in the source verse; shows the transition from God's command to Moses' action.
